primaryEvidence.claim: HLSL reflect uses incoming i; with l toward the light use reflect(-l,n).
GLSL flat provides no interpolation; smooth is perspective-correct. Modern hardware support invalidates blanket obsolete claim.
Flux W differs from incoming irradiance W/m² and directional radiance; use proper conditions for distance discussion.
Lambertian BRDF is reflectance/pi, with constant outgoing radiance; cosine weighting still occurs in transport.
Isotropy means rotating about the surface normal, not arbitrary orientation; velvet can show retroreflection.
Material reflection follows dielectric/conductor and directional Fresnel behavior.
Point lights use a positional delta and intensity/distance²; spots and projection lights are variants.
DiffuseTerm computes saturate(.5*NdotL+.5), squaring when light-warp is not used; ordinary Lambert saturates NdotL.
Official renderer separately binds light falloff and projected light textures and uses additive light interactions.
Emission affects material appearance and may contribute through configured GI; not universally unable to light surroundings.
Lightmaps use additional UVs and atlas charts; baked UV data stored in Mesh.uv2/TEXCOORD1.
Unity light probes use L2 SH with nine coefficients per channel; probes are not universally raw cubemaps.
